collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — JUSTICE AND CONSEQUENCES (JUS-01 to JUS-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Everyday rules, disputes between neighbors, the elders and the council, making things right, losing a role, a night to cool down, wrongful suspicion and evidence that doesn't add up. Consequences are proportionate and never cruel; children get guidance; nobody goes without food, water or shelter; an accusation is not guilt.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks a child aged 6-12 and an adult)

collection.description: A child carved a little fish into the big carved post at the meeting place: sand it smooth together, or offer proper lessons.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Someone has carved a little fish into the big carved post at the meeting place, right at child height. It's quite a good fish. The carvers are not pleased. (subject) has a small knife and a very guilty face. (friend), one of the carvers, has found (subject.him/her).

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (friend) shows (subject) how to rub the fish away with a smooth stone until the wood is even again. It takes all afternoon. At the end, (friend) hands (subject.him/her) a small block of wood. "Carve on this. As many fish as you like." (subject) carves twelve. Some of them are very good.

o1__text.text: (friend) shows (subject) how to rub the fish away with a smooth stone until the wood is even again. It takes all afternoon. At the end, (friend) hands (subject.him/her) a small block of wood. "Carve on this. As many fish as you like." (subject) carves twelve. Some of them are very good.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (friend) looks at the fish for a long while. Then (friend.he/she) explains that the post belongs to the whole village, not to one carver, but that the fish is good, and that (subject) can learn to carve properly if (subject.he/she) wants. (subject) starts lessons the next day. After a lot of discussion, the carvers decide the little fish can stay, since rubbing it out would leave a worse mark.
